name: Fiserv, Inc.
blurb: Fiserv is one of the world's largest financial technology companies, providing payment processing infrastructure, core banking software, and merchant services to banks, credit unions, and small businesses. Its Clover point-of-sale platform competes with Square and Toast in the small-business payments market. The stock traded under the ticker FISV on NASDAQ until June 2023, when the company transferred its listing to the NYSE and adopted the ticker FI.
recent: Fiserv lost nearly 70% of its value over the twelve months ending May 2026, falling from an all-time high of $237.79 in March 2025 to roughly $55–63 by May 2026. The collapse was triggered by a 44% single-day drop on October 29, 2025, after the company slashed its full-year earnings guidance from $10.15–$10.30 to $8.50–$8.60 per share and reported Q3 revenue of $4.9 billion against a $5.36 billion forecast. The root cause was the evaporation of Argentina-driven growth tailwinds that had masked mid-single-digit core organic growth behind double-digit reported figures. Q1 2026 results (reported May 5, 2026) showed GAAP operating margins compressing from 27.2% to 18.3% year-over-year and organic revenue declining 4%, sending the stock down an additional 8.6%. The company is in the midst of a leadership overhaul and is expected to present a recovery plan at its May 2026 investor day.
